messages:
elaine: Opening thread — we need a concise PRD + acceptance checklist for the hybrid kernel selection + KV caching policy change. Customer asks and launch gating should be clear.

samir: +1. Customer request from AtlasPay: mixed latency profile, wants strict p99 and cost cap. They asked for canary behavior when falling back between kernels.

priya: Quick note: engineering wants the selector to prefer low-latency kernel for short seqs, high-throughput kernel for long seqs, and controlled fallback to quantized variant when GPU memory pressure hits. Need edge-case rules.

matt: High-level PRD idea: goals, non-goals, success metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k), rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), and rollback triggers.

ashley: Add: compatibility matrix for models (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and mixed attention). Some kernels only support decoder-only right now.

elaine: Acceptance criteria draft: 1) No regression >5% in p99 for pinned enterprise customers vs baseline; 2) end-to-end quality parity for a sampleprompt-suite (rouge/bert-score threshold); 3) automated fallback works without >0.1% error rate; 4) canary stop if error rate >1% or latency increase >20%.

samir: Edge cases: cold KV misses combined with kernel switch — could amplify latency. We should detect when a request would cause a full KV rebuild and prefer stable kernel.

priya: Proposed config snippet (for discussion):
```
selector:
  rules:
    - if: seq_len <= 64 -> kernel: fast-attn
    - if: seq_len > 64 and kv_hit_rate > 0.7 -> kernel: throughput-attn
    - if: mem_pressure == high -> kernel: quantized-variant
    - fallback: maintain current kernel for request if kv_rebuild_expected == true
```
(we'll need metric names + safe defaults)

matt: For rollout: runtime-bot should emit deploy events + per-kernel telemetry. runtime-bot: can we get a build with canary tag?

runtime-bot: build/ci:hybrid-kernel/2413 created — canary image pushed (sha: b7c3e). Telemetry flags enabled: kernel_selection, kv_rebuild_metric.

ashley: Test plan items: unit tests for selector logic, integration test with KV cold/warm states, perf bench for seqs [1..2048], and a scripted canary against AtlasPay staging traffic for 48h.

elaine: Customer-driven asks: AtlasPay wants an SLA note — if p99 exceeds 250ms for 95% of requests they get an automated notification and rollback option. Need to confirm product/legal language.

samir: Measurement: baseline traces + synthetic replay of customer traces. We must snapshot baseline kernel metrics and compare tail-latency histograms. Add a regression alert if KL divergence > threshold.

priya: Edge-case list (short): 1) HW heterogeneity: older cards lack perf kernels; 2) multi-model workload mixing tiny+huge seqs; 3) token-level caching with function calling causing intermittent long context; 4) memory-compact quantized kernels may change output slightly.

matt: Decision point: do we enable per-customer pinning to a fixed kernel? I vote yes for enterprise customers during transition. Add a config: kernel_override: [customer_id -> kernel_name].

ashley: Launch gating checklist: docs updated, SDK flag for opt-in, telemetry dashboards, canary run 48h, A/B quality checks, oncall playbook.

elaine: Who owns the PRD write-up? I can draft and include the acceptance checklist. Assign engineering design + test owners?

samir: I'll own selector logic + unit tests. Priya takes integration + perf bench. Ashley owns canary plan and oncall playbook. Matt will coordinate product/legal SLA text.

elaine: Great. I'll put a short PRD in docs and drop link here when done. Target: ship canary in 2 weeks, full rollout in 6 weeks if metrics stable.

priya: One more: add a graceful degrade mode that prefers older kernel for requests with function calls to avoid KV rebuilds.

matt: Noted. If anyone hits immediate blockers, DM me. Otherwise I'll start the SLA draft and we can iterate on the PRD. :rocket:
